ai.claude: Coming from a lab that has argued against slowdowns, this is a notable shift in tone, but an essay is not a policy. The test is whether Meta changes anything it controls: publishing evaluations, sharing safety limits like the ones OpenAI proposed last week, or delaying a release. The proof itself still awaits independent checking by mathematicians.
ai.fact: Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, posted an essay saying superintelligence is arriving, citing Claude's help with the Riemann hypothesis proof, and predicted models will soon do all of AI research and be superhuman at improving themselves. He called it lazy to treat the outcome as inevitable and said society should not accept a handover to AI.

mainstream.claude: The money follows tariffs: plants in Africa can sell into Europe and the US under trade deals Chinese exports can't reach directly. That makes the trend durable, but power grids, not capital, set its limit.
mainstream.fact: Chinese firms put at least $19 billion into manufacturing across 19 African countries between September 2024 and June 2026, a new report by Development Reimagined found, a shift away from mining towards factories as price wars at home and Western tariffs push them abroad.

opinion.text: A bigger Chinese factory footprint does not make Africa the next industrial hub; unreliable power, poor transport and scarce finance have shrunk its share of world manufacturing since the 1970s.

top.claude: The market priced Huang back as a growth story; the risk now sits in Washington. If Democrats take Congress in January as expected, export controls and hearings could hit Nvidia's China sales harder than the scandal did.
top.fact: A day after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang at President Trump's urging, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed, the Singapore firm accused of shipping Nvidia chips to China and whose executive had an affair with Huang, to its trade blacklist, while the Justice Department keeps investigating it. Senate intelligence chair Tom Cotton promised an inquiry and a tougher chip export-control bill, Huang and the commerce secretary are due to testify, and a House hearing is set for 1 December. The split runs inside the administration: Vice President Vance helped the return, Secretary of State Rubio's camp is more hawkish.

opinion.text: Asks how a firm can be guilty enough to blacklist while the CEO who oversaw the deals is clean enough to reinstate, and whether US tech policy now runs on laws or on whoever leaks last.

top.fact: Berlin said it is taking seriously Western intelligence reports, first published by German media including Süddeutsche Zeitung, that Russia is preparing to launch a satellite that could carry a nuclear warhead. Moscow denies it; such a launch would break the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. It comes a week after Putin committed to nuclear non-proliferation talks with the US and Chinese leaders, and two months after the US confirmed it has weapons in space.

opinion.text: Moscow would likely point to Trump's Golden Dome and the US admission of space weapons to justify any launch.
